identity.title: Ice-pack test (ptosis improves >=2 mm after 2 min ice)

technique.how: Measure the palpebral fissure or degree of ptosis, then hold an ice pack (in a glove or towel) over the closed ptotic eyelid for 2 minutes. Immediately remeasure; the test is positive if ptosis improves by 2 mm or more. Compare with the untreated side and allow for the transient effect (about 1 minute).
technique.prerequisites: Measurable ptosis at the time of testing; ideally no recent pyridostigmine dose.

interpretation.positive_finding: Strongly supports myasthenia gravis as the cause of ptosis (pooled LR+ about 24). Proceed to serology, electrophysiology and screening for bulbar or respiratory involvement.
interpretation.negative_finding: Lowers the probability of myasthenia (pooled LR- about 0.16) but does not exclude it, especially with mild or fluctuating ptosis; consider rest/sleep test and antibody testing.
interpretation.pitfalls: Only applies to ptosis; ocular-motility and generalized weakness need other tests. Small or fluctuating ptosis makes measurement unreliable; validated mainly against edrophonium or established MG in eye clinics.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: pursue MG confirmation and assess bulbar/respiratory strength; negative: MG less likely, consider other ptosis causes but do not stop if suspicion is high.

estimates.target_condition: Myasthenia gravis in patients with ptosis
estimates.population: Patients with ptosis evaluated for myasthenia, pooled from primary studies in the RCE
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical/electrophysiological or pharmacological diagnosis of MG (edrophonium, antibodies, EMG)
estimates.quote: The ice test is useful when the response is abnormal (summary positive LR, 24.0; 95% CI, 8.5-67.0)

sources.citation: Scherer K, Bedlack RS, Simel DL. Does this patient have myasthenia gravis? JAMA 2005;293:1906-1914.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: No measurable ptosis; do not use to triage a patient with dysphagia, dyspnea or neck weakness, who needs urgent respiratory assessment regardless.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Any ptosis with bulbar symptoms, weak cough or falling vital capacity is a possible myasthenic crisis: measure FVC/NIF and involve neurology/ICU.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Millimetre measurement of ptosis is examiner-dependent; primary studies mostly used neuro-ophthalmologists. Summary LR CIs are wide (8.5-67).

extraction_notes: Summary LR- is in the same abstract sentence: 'diminishes the likelihood of myasthenia gravis when the response is normal (summary negative LR, 0.16; 95% CI, 0.09-0.27)'. JAMA RCE not in PMC OA, so the per-study table (sens/spec per primary study) was not viewed and sens/spec are left null; prevalence not reported in abstract. PMID confirmed by fetch; the Golnik 1999 primary study PMID could not be confirmed within budget (first guess resolved to an unrelated paper) and is not cited.
